title: Almond Milk Granita
changes_from_base: Almond paste dissolved in milk and water replaces the strawberry purée, with a pinch of cinnamon and toasted almonds to serve.
summary: This refreshing frozen dessert combines smooth almond milk with a hint of cinnamon and crunchy toasted almonds for a light texture.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Place 960 ml water, 400 g almond paste and 540 ml whole milk into a large saucepan and heat gently. Mash the paste pieces with a potato masher to help them dissolve.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat as soon as the liquid starts to steam, before it boils. Leave it to cool slightly.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Use a stick blender to process the warm mixture until it is completely smooth. Pour the liquid into a muslin-lined sieve over a large bowl and let it drip through without pressing.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Stir a pinch of ground cinnamon into the cooled liquid and pour it into a 33 x 23 cm metal tin. Place the tin in the freezer until the edges start to become icy.

steps.title: Break
steps.text: After about 30 min, use the back of a large spoon to break the icy edges into smaller pieces. Repeat this process several times over 2 h until the mixture forms frozen shards.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Layer some of the 60 g toasted flaked almonds into 8 glasses and fill with the granita. Finish each glass with a final topping of the remaining almonds.

tips: Ensure the almond paste is fully dissolved for the smoothest possible texture.
Use a metal tin to help the liquid freeze more quickly and evenly.
Toast the flaked almonds until golden to provide a nutty contrast to the icy granita.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer up to 1 week; fork it again before serving.
